body: Iran warns of tougher response: Oil, gold and stocks to watch over the holiday weekend Iran's latest warning puts oil supplies and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz back in focus for traders. Crude oil is the most direct market to watch, followed by gold and stock-index futures. Bitcoin and Ethereum can provide an earlier weekend indication of risk appetite, although their movements cannot reliably predict Tuesday's stock-market direction. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said new attacks on the country would "meet a faster, heavier and more painful response". Reuters separately reported his warning that further attacks would bring a stronger response. Reuters The warning followed U.S. Central Command's statement that American forces struck three Iranian crude-oil tankers on Saturday after Iranian ballistic-missile attacks on two U.S. Navy ships. CENTCOM said no American personnel were injured. Reuters According to an Al Jazeera update, the IRGC also said it attacked three U.S.-affiliated vessels and three oil tankers using what it described as an unauthorised route through Hormuz. title: Oman's Total Credit Growth Eases Slightly to 12.5% in July YoY
body: Oman's total credit growth moderated marginally in July 2026, with the year-over-year rate easing to 12.5%, down from 12.7% in June 2026. The figures, updated on 06 September 2026, reflect a still-robust expansion in lending activity, albeit at a slightly slower pace than the previous month. Both the current and previous readings compare each month's credit growth to the same month a year earlier, indicating that while credit momentum remains strong, the rapid acceleration seen earlier in the year may be stabilising. The July data suggest that Oman's financial system continues to support economic activity, even as the pace of expansion in total credit shows signs of gradual cooling. title: Oman's M2 Money Supply Growth Eases to 14.9% in July 2026
body: Oman's broad money supply (M2) growth edged lower in July 2026, with the year-over-year rate slowing to 14.9%, down from 15.4% in June 2026. The figures, updated on 06 September 2026, indicate a modest deceleration in liquidity expansion within the Sultanate's financial system. Both the current and previous readings are based on year-over-year comparisons, measuring changes in M2 for each month against the same month a year earlier. While money supply growth remains elevated, the slight easing in July suggests a marginal cooling in the pace of monetary expansion after June's stronger annual increase.
